title: Naturality of the first Tor identification with the ideal-tensor kernel
statement: Let $f:R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $I\subseteq R$ an ideal, $J=IA\subseteq A$ the ideal generated by $f(I)$, $M$ an $R$-module, $N$ an $A$-module, and $g:M\to N$ an additive map with $g(rx)=f(r)g(x)$ for all $r\in R$, $x\in M$. Write $\mu_R:I\otimes_RM\to M$, $a\otimes x\mapsto ax$, $\mu_A:J\otimes_AN\to N$, $b\otimes y\mapsto by$, and $\theta:I\otimes_RM\to J\otimes_AN$, $a\otimes x\mapsto f(a)\otimes g(x)$. Let $\cdots\to P_1\xrightarrow{d_1}P_0\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}M\to0$ be a resolution of $M$ by free $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-free-module] and $\cdots\to G_1\xrightarrow{e_1}G_0\xrightarrow{\eta}N\to0$ a resolution of $N$ by free $A$-modules, and compute $\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(M,R/I)=H_1(P_\bullet\otimes_RR/I)$ and $\operatorname{Tor}^A_1(N,A/J)=H_1(G_\bullet\otimes_AA/J)$ with them [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. (a) (Stacks 00M6.) There is an injective $R$-linear map $\partial_R:\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(M,R/I)\to I\otimes_RM$ with image $\ker\mu_R$, given as follows: for a cycle $z\in P_1\otimes_RR/I=P_1/IP_1$ choose $y\in P_1$ lifting $z$; then $d_1(y)\in IP_0$, say $d_1(y)=\sum_ka_kp_k$ with $a_k\in I$, $p_k\in P_0$, and $\partial_R[z]=\sum_ka_k\otimes\varepsilon(p_k)$ (independent of the choices). Likewise $\partial_A:\operatorname{Tor}^A_1(N,A/J)\to J\otimes_AN$ is injective with image $\ker\mu_A$. (b) (Naturality.) There are additive maps $\varphi_n:P_n\to G_n$ with $\varphi_n(rp)=f(r)\varphi_n(p)$, $e_n\varphi_n=\varphi_{n-1}d_n$ ($n\ge1$) and $\eta\varphi_0=g\varepsilon$. For any such $\varphi$, the maps $P_n/IP_n\to G_n/JG_n$, $p\bmod IP_n\mapsto\varphi_n(p)\bmod JG_n$, form a chain map $P_\bullet\otimes_RR/I\to G_\bullet\otimes_AA/J$; the map $\tau:\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(M,R/I)\to\operatorname{Tor}^A_1(N,A/J)$ it induces on $H_1$ (the change-of-rings map) satisfies $\partial_A\circ\tau=\theta\circ\partial_R$. Thus $\theta(\ker\mu_R)\subseteq\ker\mu_A$, and under the identifications of (a) the map $\tau$ is the restriction of $\theta$ to the kernels; in particular $\tau$ does not depend on the choice of $\varphi$.

source.place: Algebra, Remark Tag 00M6 (remark-Tor-ring-mod-ideal, lines 18690--18696), with the functoriality required in the hypothesis and proof of Lemma Tag 00MO (lemma-another-variant-local-criterion-flatness, lines 23921--23969); naturality follows from the morphism of the two ideal short exact sequences

proof.text: Short exact rows. Each $P_n$ is free, hence projective [lem-weil-pbc-free-module-projective], hence flat [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat]. Tensoring the exact sequence $0\to I\to R\to R/I\to0$ with $P_n$ gives the exact sequence $0\to P_n\otimes_RI\xrightarrow{\lambda_n}P_n\otimes_RR=P_n\to P_n\otimes_RR/I\to0$: injectivity of $\lambda_n$ ($p\otimes a\mapsto ap$) by flatness [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], exactness at $P_n$ and surjectivity by right exactness [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact]. So $\lambda_n$ is an isomorphism onto $IP_n$ and $P_n\otimes_RR/I=P_n/IP_n$. The maps $d_n\otimes1$ make the three columns complexes and the squares commute. The same holds for $G_n$ over $A$ with $J$: $0\to G_n\otimes_AJ\xrightarrow{\lambda'_n}G_n\to G_n/JG_n\to0$ exact, $\lambda'_n$ an isomorphism onto $JG_n$.

source.place: proof of Lemma 00M5, lines 18675--18684, and of Lemma 00M0 (the resolution of M tensored with 0 -> I -> R -> R/I -> 0)

proof.text: The cokernels. Tensoring the exact sequence $P_1\xrightarrow{d_1}P_0\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}M\to0$ with $I$ [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] gives $\operatorname{coker}(d_1\otimes1_I:P_1\otimes I\to P_0\otimes I)\cong M\otimes_RI$, $[p\otimes a]\mapsto\varepsilon(p)\otimes a$; composing with the symmetry $M\otimes_RI\cong I\otimes_RM$ we get $c_R:\operatorname{coker}(d_1\otimes1_I)\xrightarrow{\sim}I\otimes_RM$, $[p\otimes a]\mapsto a\otimes\varepsilon(p)$. Also $\varepsilon$ induces $\operatorname{coker}(d_1)=P_0/d_1P_1\cong M$, as the resolution is exact at $P_0$ and $\varepsilon$ is onto. Under these isomorphisms the map $\operatorname{coker}(d_1\otimes1_I)\to\operatorname{coker}(d_1)$ induced by $\lambda_0$ is $\mu_R$, since $[p\otimes a]\mapsto[ap]\mapsto a\varepsilon(p)=\mu_R(a\otimes\varepsilon(p))$. The same for $G$, giving $c_A$ and $\mu_A$.

source.place: proof of Lemma 00M5, line 18686 ('obviously M (x)_R R = M')

proof.text: Proof of (a). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-snake-lemma-modules] ($\Lambda=R$) to the diagram with top row $P_1\otimes I\xrightarrow{\lambda_1}P_1\to P_1/IP_1\to0$ (exact, Step 1), bottom row $0\to P_0\otimes I\xrightarrow{\lambda_0}P_0\to P_0/IP_0$ (exact, Step 1) and vertical maps $\alpha=d_1\otimes1_I$, $\beta=d_1$, $\gamma=\bar d_1$. Here $\ker\gamma=Z_1$ is the module of $1$-cycles of $P_\bullet\otimes R/I$, and the snake map $\partial:Z_1\to\operatorname{coker}\alpha$ is: lift $z$ to $y\in P_1$, write $d_1y=\lambda_0(w)$, $\partial z=[w]$; with $w=\sum p_k\otimes a_k$ this is $d_1y=\sum a_kp_k$. Exactness of $\ker\beta\to\ker\gamma\xrightarrow{\partial}\operatorname{coker}\alpha\to\operatorname{coker}\beta$: (i) $\ker\beta=\ker d_1=d_2P_2$ (the resolution is exact at $P_1$), whose image in $P_1/IP_1$ is exactly the module of boundaries $B_1=\bar d_2(P_2/IP_2)$; so $\ker\partial=B_1$ and $\partial$ induces an injective $R$-linear map $H_1(P_\bullet\otimes R/I)\to\operatorname{coker}\alpha$; (ii) its image is the kernel of $\operatorname{coker}\alpha\to\operatorname{coker}\beta$. Put $\partial_R=c_R\circ\partial\circ\iota$, where $\iota:\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,R/I)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_1(P_\bullet\otimes R/I)$ is the identification of [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. By Step 2, $\partial_R$ is injective with image $\ker\mu_R$, and $\partial_R[z]=c_R[\sum p_k\otimes a_k]=\sum a_k\otimes\varepsilon(p_k)$, independent of the choices by the snake lemma. The same argument over $A$ gives $\partial_A$.

source.place: proof of Lemma 00M5, lines 18675--18688 (the exact sequence Tor_1(M,R) = 0 -> Tor_1(M,R/I) -> M (x) I -> M), and Remark 00M6

proof.text: The lift $\varphi$. Regard $N$ and the $G_n$ as $R$-modules through $f$ ($r\cdot y=f(r)y$); then $g:M\to N$ is $R$-linear, $\cdots\to G_1\to G_0\xrightarrow{\eta}N\to0$ is an exact sequence of $R$-modules, and $P_\bullet\to M$ is a complex of free $R$-modules over $M$. By [lem-weil-pbc-free-complex-maps-to-resolution] there are $R$-linear $\varphi_n:P_n\to G_n$ with $\eta\varphi_0=g\varepsilon$ and $e_n\varphi_n=\varphi_{n-1}d_n$; $R$-linearity for the restricted structure is $\varphi_n(rp)=f(r)\varphi_n(p)$.

source.place: Lemma 00LS (lemma-compare-resolutions, line 17500), as used for the functoriality of Tor (lines 18598--18620)

proof.text: Induced maps. Let $\varphi$ be as in (b). For $a\in I$, $\varphi_n(ap)=f(a)\varphi_n(p)\in JG_n$, so $\bar\varphi_n:P_n/IP_n\to G_n/JG_n$ is well defined, and $\bar e_n\bar\varphi_n=\bar\varphi_{n-1}\bar d_n$ since $e_n\varphi_n=\varphi_{n-1}d_n$: a chain map, inducing $H_1(\bar\varphi)$ and $\tau=\iota_G^{-1}H_1(\bar\varphi)\iota$. The map $\psi_n:P_n\otimes_RI\to G_n\otimes_AJ$, $p\otimes a\mapsto\varphi_n(p)\otimes f(a)$, is well defined: it is biadditive and $\varphi_n(rp)\otimes f(a)=\varphi_n(p)\otimes f(r)f(a)=\varphi_n(p)\otimes f(ra)$. One has $\lambda'_n\psi_n=\varphi_n\lambda_n$ (both send $p\otimes a$ to $f(a)\varphi_n(p)$) and $(e_n\otimes1)\psi_n=\psi_{n-1}(d_n\otimes1)$. On cokernels, $c_A[\psi_0(p\otimes a)]=f(a)\otimes\eta\varphi_0(p)=f(a)\otimes g(\varepsilon(p))=\theta(c_R[p\otimes a])$. Finally $\mu_A\theta=g\mu_R$ on generators: $f(a)g(x)=g(ax)$.

source.place: hypothesis (3) of Lemma 00MO (lines 23933--23944): the map Tor_1^R(M,R/I) -> Tor_1^{R'}(M',R'/I')

proof.text: Proof of (b). Let $z\in Z_1$ (for $P$), and choose $y\in P_1$ lifting $z$ and $w\in P_0\otimes I$ with $\lambda_0(w)=d_1y$, so $\partial[z]=[w]$ (Step 3). By Step 5, $\varphi_1(y)\in G_1$ lifts $\bar\varphi_1(z)$, which is a cycle, and $\lambda'_0(\psi_0w)=\varphi_0\lambda_0(w)=\varphi_0d_1y=e_1\varphi_1(y)$. These are admissible choices in the formula of [lem-weil-pbc-snake-lemma-modules] for $G$, whose value does not depend on the choices; hence $\partial^G[\bar\varphi_1z]=[\psi_0w]$. Applying $c_A$ and Step 5, $\partial_A\tau(\iota^{-1}[z])=c_A[\psi_0w]=\theta(c_R[w])=\theta\partial_R(\iota^{-1}[z])$. So $\partial_A\tau=\theta\partial_R$. Since $\partial_R,\partial_A$ are injective with images $\ker\mu_R,\ker\mu_A$ (Step 3), $\theta$ maps $\ker\mu_R$ into $\ker\mu_A$ and $\tau=\partial_A^{-1}\circ\theta|_{\ker\mu_R}\circ\partial_R$, which does not involve $\varphi$.

The statement was made self-contained: the identification of (a) and the change-of-rings map of (b) are now defined explicitly (free resolutions, semilinear lift phi), and (b) adds that tau is independent of phi; the meaning of the old statement is kept. Proof in six steps: flatness of free modules gives short exact rows; right exactness identifies the cokernels with I(x)M and M; the snake lemma gives the injective connecting map with image ker mu (00M6); Lemma 00LS (node free-complex-maps-to-resolution, over R through f) gives the semilinear lift; the induced maps are checked; naturality follows from the choice-independence of the snake formula. No new nodes; all cited nodes are in unit sk-thm-p1 (five Mathlib leaves, one split node).
